honest_caveats: Tests at TRIVIAL level: t < 500 Myr, low sigma/m - original sweep showed disruption at t > 320 Myr
Benchmarks run with N=1024 particles per halo (~100x below publication-grade)
SIDM kernel is uniform Gaussian perturbation, not Rutherford-like pairwise
Static halo test depends on Ph4 integrator stability over 1 Gyr
These benchmarks PASS but don't yet validate in the disrupting regime where sigma/m_peak = 3.07 was derived
interpretation: All 3 benchmarks PASS at the trivial level. The simulation: (1) has a stable integrator, (2) preserves collisionless halos through fly-through encounters, (3) gives the right monotonic SIDM vs collisionless ordering. These are NECESSARY conditions for validity but not SUFFICIENT. The original sweep (which found sigma/m_peak = 3.07 cm^2/g) operates in the regime where halos ARE disrupted at t > 320 Myr; that regime needs separate validation against analytic tidal-stripping predictions or against SASHIMI published results.
